properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 9:37PM PDT until October 13 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 10 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.90 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 1:49PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W is currently rated as "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center, meaning tropical cyclone development is likely, but
beyond 24 hours. It's currently located west of Ujae near 9.3N
164.4E. It continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east-northest of Pohnpei.

Inflow into the developing disturbance will allow for locally heavy
rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per hour rain rates probable
from time to time. Rainfall totals will likely be 2 to 5 inches
tonight through Thursday, with locally higher amounts possible.
Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 30 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS TONIGHT THROUGH THURSDAY, POSSIBLY LONGER

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 8:40PM PDT until October 13 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and elevated surf are expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be expected
near times of high tide.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There
is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around
7.1 to 7.3 feet on Tuesday morning. A Beach Hazards Statement
may be issued on future shifts to follow the Coastal Flood
Advisory due to minor tidal overflow from continued elevated
tides and surf into at least Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

should prepare for very steep seas and consider remaining in port
until conditions improve.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 10:20PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Buncombe and Henderson Counties.

.Excessive runoff from a widespread 4 to 5 inch storm total rainfall
will maintain flooding along the French Broad River.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage. The French Broad
River has exceeded bankfull at the gauge site. Isolated farmland
flooding is expected across the French Broad River Valley from
Etowah downstream to Avery Creek upstream of the gauge site. At
10.7 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues. Butler Bridge Road is
inundated with up to 6 inches of floodwaters from the French Broad
River, forcing road closure.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 10.7 feet and falling.
- Forecast...The river is expected to start falling slowly
overnight, and fall to 9 ft feet Friday evening.
- Action/Advisory Stage is 10.0 feet.
- Minor Flood Stage is 13.0 feet.
properties.instruction:

alternative route. Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

EDT.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 6:14PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Thursday into the weekend, a series of low pressure systems will
move toward Southeast Alaska, bringing widespread moderate to heavy
rainfall and gale force winds to the Gulf. Strong winds are also
expected for coastal and southern panhandle communities. While the
exact timing and impacts of the system are still being refined,
confidence is continuing to increase that this will be a more
impactful system for Southeast Alaska.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
developing situation and update our forecast.
